note: Leaps practised four ways: sung over a drone, recognised by ear, met inside a tune picked by filter, then a short run to loosen up. The ear block's set is exactly the two intervals the text names.

exercise.title: 4ths and 5ths, by voice and by ear
exercise.focus: Leaps of a 4th and 5th in F · a medium tune with 4ths · a five-note run
exercise.why: A leap is easy to sing once you can hear where it lands before you sing it.

sections.text: Leaps go wrong when you guess the landing note; hearing it first makes them land.
Press Play on the drone. Sing {{1}} up to {{4}} and back, then {{1}} up to {{5}} and back, on "la". Hear the landing note in your head before you sing it. Then mix them: {{1}} {{5}} {{4}} {{1}}.
Name each interval you hear, a perfect 4th or a perfect 5th, then sing it back before you answer. Done at ten right in a row.
Look at the tune before you hear it and sing it from the staff first. Then press Play to check, and sing it with the mic until a take is clean.
Sing the run lightly on "ah", each pass a semitone higher. Keep it soft; stop before it strains.
